successCriteria.description: The ILeaveRequestService interface declares all six operations (submit, approve, reject, cancel, getById, getByEmployee) with the actor/approver role union types threaded as explicit parameters, and the LeaveRequestService class implements that interface.

submit rejects a past startDate and an endDate-before-startDate with a typed ValidationError before any repository call; it also rejects a weekend-only range (zero business days) with a ValidationError.
submit enforces RBAC: an employee actor may only submit a request whose employeeId equals their own actorId (else ApproverNotAuthorizedError); manager and hr_admin actors may submit for any employee.

submit computes business days via countBusinessDays with an empty holidays array, derives fiscalYear as the calendar year of startDate, independently recomputes remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays (not trusting a stored derived field), and throws InsufficientBalanceError when remainingDays is less than the computed business days.

submit atomically increments usedDays on the LeaveBalance (updateUsedDays called with usedDays + businessDays) and transitions the request to SUBMITTED via the repository; it does NOT auto-approve even when the employee has no manager.

submit enforces minimumNoticeDays from the LeavePolicy: when the policy defines a positive minimumNoticeDays and the gap between today and startDate is shorter, submit throws a ValidationError; undefined or zero minimumNoticeDays skips the check.
approve sets status to APPROVED, sets approvedBy and approvedAt, and does NOT call updateUsedDays (balance is untouched on approval).

approve and reject enforce approver authorization: when employee.managerId is null only hr_admin may act; otherwise approverId must equal employee.managerId. Any mismatch throws ApproverNotAuthorizedError (including a manager acting on a manager-less employee and an hr_admin acting on an employee who has a manager).
approve and reject only operate on a request whose current status is SUBMITTED; any other status throws a ValidationError, and a non-existent request throws LeaveRequestNotFoundError.

reject restores usedDays on the LeaveBalance (decrement by the request's business days, floored at zero) and sets status to REJECTED; if no balance row exists the status change still succeeds without throwing.

cancel only permits cancellation of a request in SUBMITTED or APPROVED status (DRAFT/REJECTED/CANCELLED throw ValidationError); an employee actor may cancel only their own request (else ApproverNotAuthorizedError) while manager/hr_admin may cancel any.

cancel restores usedDays (decrement by business days, floored at zero) only when the prior status was SUBMITTED; when the prior status was APPROVED, usedDays is NOT touched. A missing balance row does not cause cancel to throw.
getById returns the LeaveRequest or null, and getByEmployee delegates to the repository and returns the array (empty when none) — both are pure pass-throughs with no authorization logic.

The leave-request barrel (index.ts) re-exports the service interface, the service class, and all four custom error classes (InsufficientBalanceError, ApproverNotAuthorizedError, ValidationError, LeaveRequestNotFoundError).

The Jest test suite under tests/unit/modules/leave-request/leave-request.service.test.ts mocks all four repository dependencies and covers every method's happy path and error paths (insufficient balance, unauthorized approver, past startDate, end-before-start, weekend-only range, missing employee/policy/balance, wrong-status approve/reject/cancel, non-existent request, no-manager escalation).

constraints: All cross-module imports go through barrel index.ts files only (AGENTS.md rule 1); the service imports ILeaveBalanceRepository from ../leave-balance, IEmployeeRepository from ../employee, ILeavePolicyRepository from ../leave-policy — never from internal module files.
No use of `any` (HARNESS no-any rule, severity high); use `unknown` with type guards instead. Strict TypeScript with noImplicitAny and strict null checks must pass (tsc --noEmit).

All database access goes through repository interfaces (GP-001); the service must never touch the pg Pool or write SQL directly — it calls only ILeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository, IEmployeeRepository, and ILeavePolicyRepository methods.

RBAC is enforced inside the service, not deferred to the controller (GP-005); the actor/approver role is an explicit parameter on submit/approve/reject/cancel and the service throws a typed authorization error on violation — the service never reads ambient/auth-middleware state.
Audit records (GP-002) and notifications are NOT integrated in this phase — they are deferred to Phase 10; the service must not depend on IAuditService or INotificationService yet.
Test files follow the project Jest convention: *.test.ts under tests/, matching the configured testMatch; do not use .spec.ts and do not alter the Jest config.

remainingDays is never written directly by the service; it is independently recomputed as totalEntitlement - usedDays at submit time rather than trusting the repository's derived field, defending against stale values.

Business-day counting uses the shared countBusinessDays helper with an empty holidays array for this phase; dates are compared by calendar-date equality in UTC (normalized to UTC midnight), and the end day is EXCLUSIVE (a Mon–Fri range counts 4 days).
outOfScope: Fastify controller and routes for the leave-request API surface (Phase 8) — the service exposes its interface only; no HTTP layer is built in this phase.
Audit logging (GP-002) and notification dispatch on submit/approve/reject/cancel — deferred to Phase 10; no IAuditService or INotificationService dependency in this phase.
LeavePolicyService and LeaveBalanceService implementations (Phase 10) — this phase uses the repository interfaces directly, not the service-layer wrappers.
Public-holiday calendar integration — countBusinessDays is called with an empty holidays array in this phase; the holidays table/repository arrives in a later phase.

Input validation at the API boundary (GP-003 HTTP-level 400 responses) — that is the controller's responsibility in Phase 8; this phase's service performs domain-level validation and throws typed errors.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is strictly DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED) → CANCELLED; the service creates via repository (always DRAFT) then transitions to SUBMITTED. approve/reject require the current status to be SUBMITTED; cancel requires SUBMITTED or APPROVED; DRAFT/REJECTED/CANCELLED are terminal or non-cancellable and reject any further transition with a ValidationError.

usedDays is the denormalized source-of-truth counter: incremented atomically on submit (deduct-on-submission), decremented on reject and on cancel-from-SUBMITTED, and NOT changed on approve or cancel-from-APPROVED. A decrement is floored at zero. remainingDays is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays and is never written by the service.

An employee actor may only act on a request whose employeeId equals their own actorId (submit and cancel); manager and hr_admin actors may act on any employee's request. For approve/reject, when the owning employee's managerId is null only hr_admin is authorized; otherwise the approverId must equal the employee's managerId. Every violation throws ApproverNotAuthorizedError.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: employee actor may only submit when actorId === dto.employeeId; manager/hr_admin may submit for any employee.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: ValidationError for past startDate, end-before-start, weekend-only/zero-business-day range, missing employee/policy/balance, or unmet minimumNoticeDays; InsufficientBalanceError when recomputed remainingDays < business days; ApproverNotAuthorizedError when an employee submits for another employee.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: When employee.managerId is null only approverRole 'hr_admin' is authorized; otherwise approverId must equal employee.managerId. Request must be in SUBMITTED status.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveRequestNotFoundError when the request does not exist; ValidationError when status is not SUBMITTED; ApproverNotAuthorizedError for any approver mismatch. Does NOT modify usedDays.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Same authorization rule as approve: hr_admin only when managerId is null, else approverId === employee.managerId. Request must be in SUBMITTED status.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveRequestNotFoundError when absent; ValidationError when status is not SUBMITTED; ApproverNotAuthorizedError on mismatch. Restores usedDays (decrement by business days, floored at zero); a missing balance row does not cause failure.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: employee actor may cancel only their own request (actorId === employeeId); manager/hr_admin may cancel any. Request must be in SUBMITTED or APPROVED status.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveRequestNotFoundError when absent; ValidationError when status is DRAFT/REJECTED/CANCELLED; ApproverNotAuthorizedError when an employee cancels another's request. Restores usedDays only if prior status was SUBMITTED; a missing balance row does not cause failure.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No authorization enforced at the service layer — pure read pass-through to the repository (RBAC for read visibility is the controller's concern in Phase 8).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the LeaveRequest or null; never throws on a missing record.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No authorization enforced at the service layer — pure read pass-through; RBAC scoping is the controller's concern in Phase 8.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the array of the employee's requests (empty when none); delegates directly to the repository.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Business-day counting must reuse the shared countBusinessDays(startDate, endDate, holidays) helper, which normalizes dates to UTC midnight, excludes weekends and the provided holidays, and treats the end day as EXCLUSIVE (Mon–Fri = 4 days). The service must call it with an empty holidays array and must not reimplement day-counting logic.

The service must use ILeaveRequestRepository exactly as declared: create(dto) inserts as DRAFT, then updateStatus(id, status, approvedBy?, approvedAt?) transitions the status; findById and findByEmployee are the read paths. The service must not bypass these methods or assume a different repository shape.

Balance operations must use ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear) for lookup and updateUsedDays(id, usedDays) for mutation — the service uses the repository directly (not ILeaveBalanceService), consistent with the settled Phase 7 dependency decision. remainingDays on the returned LeaveBalance is a derived field the service must NOT trust; it recomputes totalEntitlement - usedDays itself.

The service must operate on the LeaveRequest and CreateLeaveRequestDto shapes exactly as defined in the model; submit accepts CreateLeaveRequestDto and all methods return LeaveRequest (or null/array for reads). The status field uses the LeaveRequestStatus enum from shared types.

The deduct-on-submission / restore-on-reject / restore-on-cancel-from-SUBMITTED (not from APPROVED) / no-change-on-approve balance semantics, calendar-year fiscalYear, business-days-only exclusive-end counting, and manager-less escalation-to-hr_admin rules must match the binding business_rules in reconciled.json exactly — the implementation must not diverge from these settled decisions.

The barrel must re-export the service interface (ILeaveRequestService), the service class (LeaveRequestService), and all four error classes (InsufficientBalanceError, ApproverNotAuthorizedError, ValidationError, LeaveRequestNotFoundError) so downstream Phase 8 controller and Phase 10 audit integration can import them through the public entry point only.

integrationPoints.why: submit deducts usedDays and reject/cancel-from-SUBMITTED restore usedDays by calling findByEmployeeAndPolicy and updateUsedDays on the balance repository directly.
submit, approve, and reject look up the owning Employee via findById to validate existence and to read managerId for RBAC authorization and manager-less escalation.
submit looks up the LeavePolicy via findById to enforce minimumNoticeDays before deducting balance.
submit, reject, and cancel-from-SUBMITTED all compute the request's business-day count via the shared helper to drive balance deduction/restoration.
The service references LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED for all status transitions and guards.
